content.intro: {state} has no sales tax on a vehicle. Instead you pay an infrastructure maintenance fee of {stateRate} of the price, capped at a top amount, plus a title fee and a two-year registration fee.

howItWorks.text: The infrastructure maintenance fee is {stateRate} of the gross proceeds of the sale, up to a maximum. The value of a trade-in is not part of the gross proceeds.
A sale that pays the fee is exempt from state and local sales and use taxes, so no county or city tax is added on top.
A vehicle first registered in another state and later registered here by the same owner pays a flat fee, not a percentage.
Counties bill a yearly property tax on vehicles, and you must pay it before registering. It is not part of this total.

faq.q: Is there a sales tax on cars in South Carolina?
faq.text: No. Vehicles pay an infrastructure maintenance fee instead, which is a percentage of the price with a maximum amount.

faq.q: Does a trade-in lower the fee?
faq.text: Yes. The fee is figured on the gross proceeds of the sale, which the DOR guide defines as not including the value of any trade-in.

faq.q: Is the county property tax included?
faq.text: No. It is billed by your county and depends on the vehicle's value, and it must be paid before you register.
